subject: SKU harmonization & credit smoothing for observability add-ons
messages:
From: Alicia Park <apark@brightlane.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightlane Procurement <procurement@brightlane.com>
Date: Mon, 14 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability add-ons - harmonizing SKUs & credits

Hi Connor,

Thanks for the demo last week — the dashboard previews were really helpful. Before we move to procurement, procurement needs a clearer picture of how you expect us to purchase the observability add-ons (retention, tracing, advanced dashboards). Two specific asks: 

1) SKU harmonization: Our finance team prefers a simpler SKU (single add-on SKU with optional tiers) versus multiple small SKUs per feature. Can you outline a practical mapping from your current SKUs to a consolidated bundle?

2) Credit smoothing: We have bursty ingestion patterns. Rather than strict per-GB overage, would you consider a smoothing/credit pool that amortizes peaks across the month? If so, how would that affect list pricing and discount mechanics for an annual commitment?

Target timeline: procurement wants final commercial terms by May 25 so we can hit Q2 ACV targets. We expect ~100TB retained (30-day window), 2M traces/month, and 10 advanced-dashboard seats in year 1.

Appreciate any worked examples.

Best,
Alicia Park
VP Engineering, Brightlane
apark@brightlane.com

Attachments: (none in this message)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Park <apark@brightlane.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 May 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons - harmonizing SKUs & credits

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear asks. Internal cc for pricing + commercial.

Short answers up front: yes, we can present a consolidated SKU mapping and offer a credit-smoothing construct for bursty ingestion tied to a committed annual spend. Below is a practical mapping and a worked example based on the numbers you sent. I attached a draft pricing_model.xlsx with blended maths.

Proposed SKU mapping (high level):
- OBS-BUNDLE (base): includes core retention (30d, up to baseline TB), basic tracing (ingest + indexing), and 5 basic dashboards
- OBS-RETENTION-ADD (tiered): per-GB add for retention beyond baseline
- OBS-TRACE-CREDITS: pool of trace credits consumed at a per-trace rate; excess billed at a blended overage rate
- OBS-ADV-DASH: per-seat license for advanced dashboards above base seats

Credit smoothing concept: create a monthly "smoothing pool" based on committed baseline of 100TB/2M traces. Bursts above daily threshold draw from the pool; once pool exhausted, standard overage rates apply. The pool is replenished monthly.

Worked example (from pricing_model.xlsx):
- Annual commit: $240k (list: $300k across add-ons)
- Commit includes: 100TB retention baseline, 2M trace credits, 10 ADV-DASH seats
- Smoothing pool: 20% buffer of baseline (20TB / 400k trace credits)
- Discount mechanics: discount applied to list bundle price; overage rates reduced by 10% when smoothing pool included in commit

Next steps: Ben & Marissa can confirm discount frameworks and whether the smoothing pool should be treated as an included entitlement or an optional purchased add-on. If acceptable, we'll turn this into a short SOW and finalize procurement language.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com

Attachments: pricing_model.xlsx (spreadsheet, 54KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 May 2028 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons - harmonizing SKUs & credits (internal)

Connor — quick internal recommendation before we send a formal response to Brightlane.

1) Discount framework: for a $240k annual commit, we can start at 18% off list for the OBS-BUNDLE. If they want the smoothing pool treated as an included entitlement, reduce to 15% (because pool has carry value). Alternatively, keep 18% but cap smoothing pool size to 15% of baseline.

2) Overage pricing: propose blended overage rates that are 10% below published list when customer purchases the smoothing pool. This is a strong commercial signal and easier for procurement to model.

3) Advanced dashboards: for 10 seats, offer 2 seats standard in bundle, price the remaining 8 at $350/seat/mo list. Offer seat-volume discount: 20% at commit.

4) Operational clause: we need a clause in the SOW that allows us to re-evaluate smoothing pool sizing after Q1 usage data; this protects us from sustained high usage masquerading as bursts.

If you want to be aggressive to close in Q2, we can front-load two one-time onboarding credits (totaling $5k) and sign a 12-month SOW with an auto-renew.

Ben
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

(Internal note: deal id BL-2028-1382 tracked in HubSpot. Pricing worksheet updated.)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Brightlane Procurement <procurement@brightlane.com>
Date: Thu, 18 May 2028 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons - harmonizing SKUs & credits

Hi Alicia — following internal alignment, here is a concise commercial proposal you can circulate to procurement. Happy to hop on a call if helpful.

Proposal (summary):
- Offer: OBS-BUNDLE (includes 100TB retention baseline, 2M trace credits, 2 ADV-DASH seats) + OBS-ADV-DASH (8 additional seats)
- Annual commit: $240,000 (list value across items: $291,000)
- Discount: 15% off list when smoothing pool is included as an entitlement (we can extend to 18% if smoothing pool is purchased as a separate add-on instead of entitling it)
- Smoothing pool: 20% monthly buffer (20TB / 400k trace credits) that can absorb daily peaks; pool replenished monthly. Once pool exhausted, blended overage rates apply (10% below published overage).
- Seats: additional 8 advanced dashboard seats at $350/seat/mo list; with commit discount (15%) = $299/seat/mo; annualized seat line included in $240k commit.
- Operational guardrail: SOW contains a usage review clause at 90 days to resize the smoothing pool if average utilization stays >60% of baseline for two consecutive months.
- Onboarding credits: one-time $5,000 success credit applied at go-live (to be amortized across first invoice).

Deliverables: short SOW (attached: Brightlane_SOW_v1.pdf) and a pricing workbook (pricing_model.xlsx). Please review and let me know if procurement wants a minor reformat for PO ingestion. If this is acceptable, I'll send a DocuSign SOW next week with standard SOC2 & data handling clauses.

If helpful, available for a 30-min call tomorrow at 10am PT.

Thanks,
Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com
